To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured elastic, inelastic and transfer cross sections in the reaction of 22 Ne+208Pb at 128 MeVe, and that we have determined the C2 charge deformation parameter by a DWBA an- alysis of the experimental angular distributions, showing a strong decrease from 22Ne to 24Ne.
the reaction dynamics of 22 Ne +208 Pb at 129 MeV is dominated by the transfer of one neutron, while the one for 24 Ne+208 Pb at 180 MeV is dominated instead by transfer of one proton.

the reaction mechanism for the reaction 22 Ne + 208 Pb at E=128 MeV is dominated by direct processes, with a very small contribution of compound nucleus reactions, while for the reaction 24Ne + 208Pb at E=182 MeV the reaction mechanism is dominated by compound nucleus reactions, with a very little direct contribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the structure and reaction dynamics of the 22 Ne and the 24 Ne nuclei, which are the two most neutron-rich isotopes of the Ne isotopes chain.
the study of the reaction dynamics and nuclear structure properties of moderately neutron-rich 22 Ne and unstable 24 Ne nuclei.
the study of the reaction mechanisms in the 22 Ne+208Pb and 24Ne+208Pb reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reaction 22 Ne + 208 Pb at E = 128 MeV, in the present experimental conditions, does not allow a conclusive statement on the structure of 24 Ne, while the reaction 24 Na + 208 Pb, at E = 182 MeV, allows the determination of C 2 for the 24 Ne nucleus.
the 24 Ne nucleus has a large oblate shape, which is in line with the results obtained in the 24 Ne+208 Pb experiment.
, in the case of 24 Ne, the charge deformation parameter is reduced to about half the value of the stable isotopes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C 2 deformation parameter for 22 Ne is 0.30(4) and for 24 Ne it is 0.16(4), in agreement with the systematics.
the 22 Ne+Pb reaction is not a good tool to investigate the structure of 22 Ne, but it is a very useful tool to study the structure of the unstable 24Ne nucleus.
the 22 Ne+208Pb reaction at 128 Mev of bombarding energy is a good candidate for the production of the 24 Ne nucleus and that it can be studied with the PRISMA CLARA setup.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction dynamics is very different for the two isotopes and that the nuclear structure effects are very large, as shown by the comparison with a standard DWBA analysis.
the C 2 parameter is not constant for isotopes close to the drip line and that the reaction dynamics is not the same for stable and unstable isotopes of a given mass number.
the reaction 22 Ne + 208 Pb at E lab =128 MeV has been successfully employed as an indirect method to probe the nuclear structure properties of 24 Ne, which is not available in the laboratory.
